title: Can, Cannot and Simple Abilities
introduction: Describe abilities and ask what others can do.
definition: Describe abilities and ask what others can do.
rules: Can expresses ability; cannot expresses lack of ability.
Use the base verb after can or cannot.

examples.question: A bird can ___ (fly or flies).
steps: Use the base verb after can.

examples.question: A fish cannot ___ on land. (walk or swims)
steps: Use a base verb that describes moving on land.

exercises.question: A bird can ___ (fly or flies).
exercises.solution: Use the base verb after can.

exercises.question: A fish cannot ___ on land. (walk or swims)
exercises.solution: Use a base verb that describes moving on land.

exercises.question: ___ you draw a robot?
exercises.solution: Put can first in an ability question.

exercises.question: Can she sing? Yes, she ___.
exercises.solution: Repeat can in a positive reply.

exercises.question: Can he fly like a bird? No, he ___. (can't or isn't)
exercises.solution: Can't is the short form of cannot.

exercises.question: They can ___ a ball. (catch or catches)
exercises.solution: Do not add -es to a verb after can.

summary: Describe abilities and ask what others can do. Can expresses ability; cannot expresses lack of ability.
